result.title: Credal Machine Learning for Risk-Averse Decision Making
result.summary: In many machine learning applications, it is necessary to guard against worst-case scenarios and predictions that could result in substantial losses. In principle, this can be achieved by training risk-averse predictive models that minimize loss functions such as conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), rather than relying on models that perform well on average. In practice, however, the effectiveness of this approach to risk aversion is undermined by the learner's uncertainty regarding the true loss distribution and, consequently, the true CVaR. To achieve reliable risk-aversion, we propose a method in which this (epistemic) uncertainty is represented in terms of credal sets, i.e., sets of probability distributions. More specifically, we develop an efficient yet reliable learner that produces predictions in the form of credal sets and combine it with a novel decision rule that maps each credal set to a single predictive distribution for CVaR minimization. Across classification, under distribution shift, and in reinforcement learning, our approach reliably avoids catastrophic decisions, while sacrificing little in expected performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出用 credal sets（概率分布集合）表示学习器对真实损失分布的认识不确定性，学习以 credal set 形式输出的预测器，并设计将其映射为单一预测分布以最小化 CVaR 的决策规则，在分类、分布偏移与强化学习中避免灾难性决策。
AI.relevance_reason: 以「分布集合」而非点估计刻画认识不确定性并据此做风险规避决策，可能为 LVR 中多 latent 假设的表示、以及基于不确定性的验证与停止决策提供概念线索，具体迁移方式尚需核查。
